links.outcome: Patient trust, anxiety, second-opinion and legal intent when AI results disclosed in mammography report
links.effect: Disclosing discordant AI reduced trust in radiologist (73.0 vs 90.1; p<0.001), raised anxiety (58.0% vs 16.0%), second-opinion intent (50.0% vs 8.7%); AI approval remained >85% across groups.
links.quote: Contextualised disclosure of AI results mitigates adverse emotional and behavioural responses, supporting its use as a communication strategy in AI-integrated mammography.

links.outcome: Effect of adding explanatory note on AI limitations on patient reactions to discordant AI flag
links.effect: Explanation reduced anxiety to 25.3% (OR = 0.26); versus Radiologist Only, only modest anxiety increase (p = 0.04) and no significant trust reduction (p = 0.42).
links.quote: Adding explanatory context significantly mitigated these effects (e.g., anxiety: 25.3%; OR = 0.26).

links.outcome: trust, anxiety, second-opinion and legal intent
links.effect: Discordant AI disclosure: trust 73.0 vs 90.1; anxiety 58.0% vs 16.0%; second-opinion 50.0% vs 8.7%; legal action 60.7% vs 38.7%.
links.quote: Disclosure of a discordant AI result significantly reduced trust in the radiologist (73.0 vs 90.1; p < 0.001), and increased anxiety (58.0% vs 16.0%; OR = 15.4), second-opinion intent (50.0% vs 8.7%; OR = 10.2), and legal action consideration (60.7% vs 38.7%; OR = 2.49).
